title: Idiom
description: An English idiom the app teaches: a pointer into `entries` plus the two things a dictionary entry drops — which of its senses is the idiomatic one, and where the phrase comes from. Selected by pipeline/09_idioms.py from Wiktionary's `idiomatic` sense tag; no new text is generated for it.

senseIndex.description: Which sense of the entry is the idiomatic one. Not always 0: "peanut butter" is an idiom for spreading resources too thin, and its first sense is the spread.

tags.description: Register labels in Hindi (स्लैंग, अनौपचारिक, पुराना, ब्रिटिश…), from that sense's Wiktionary tags. Empty for a neutral phrase.

etymology.description: Wiktionary's etymology prose, in English, or empty. Shown as "the story behind it", attributed to Wiktionary.

freqRank.description: The frequency rank of the phrase's rarest word, carried over from the entry. A tie-breaker only: it rates "keep good time" above "spill the beans", so it must not order the list on its own.

weight.description: How many languages Wiktionary's editors have translated the phrase into: the evidence that a reader will actually meet it. This orders the browse list and so decides which idioms a reader is shown each day.

kind.description: `phrasal` for a verb plus particles (give up, take off), `idiom` otherwise. They are taught the same way and share a screen; the reader filters between them.
